events.title: Henry VII Marries Elizabeth of York
events.description: King Henry VII of England married Elizabeth of York, the daughter of Edward IV. The wedding joined the rival houses of Lancaster and York.
events.significance: The marriage helped end the Wars of the Roses and established the Tudor dynasty, which ruled England for more than a century.

events.title: Captain Cook Reaches Hawaii
events.description: English navigator James Cook became the first known European to reach the Hawaiian Islands. He named them the Sandwich Islands.
events.significance: The encounter opened lasting contact between Hawaii and the outside world, with profound consequences for the islands and their people.

events.title: German Empire Proclaimed at Versailles
events.description: Wilhelm I of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor, unifying the German states under Prussian leadership.
events.significance: The new German Empire reshaped the balance of power in Europe and set the stage for the tensions that led to the 20th century's world wars.

events.title: Birth of A. A. Milne
events.description: Alan Alexander Milne, the English writer who created Winnie-the-Pooh, was born in London.
events.significance: Milne's gentle stories of Pooh and his friends became some of the most beloved children's books in the world.

events.title: Paris Peace Conference Opens
events.description: Delegates from the victorious Allied powers gathered in France to begin settling the terms of peace after World War I.
events.significance: The conference produced the Treaty of Versailles and the League of Nations, shaping international relations between the wars.
